1 Important Information for Tentative Rulings and Hearings:
2
1. Please review and follow the Tentative Ruling Instructions which can be found on the Court’s website
3
using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/unified-family-court/ufc-tentative-rulings.
4
2. If you wish to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, you must notify the other party
5
(unless there is a restraining order in place) and the Court Clerk in the Department where the hearing
6
is scheduled of your objection by 4:00 PM the Court day prior to the hearing date. Court days do not
7
include Court holidays, Saturdays, or Sundays. The Court’s Holiday Schedule can be found on the
8
Court’s website using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/general-information/holiday-
9
schedules.
10
3. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 403 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
11
please call (415) 551–3741 or send an email to Department403@sftc.org.
12
4. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 404 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
13
please call (415) 551–3744 or send an email to Department404@sftc.org.
14
5. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 416 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
15
please call (415) 551– 3756 or send an email to Department416@sftc.org.
16
6. When you contact the Court Clerk to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, please
17
specify the paragraph(s) and / or line number(s) of the Tentative Ruling which contains the language
18
to which you object.
19
7. You may appear at your hearing either (a) in-person; (b) by video; or (c) by phone. Pursuant to SFLR
20
11.7(D)(4), if you choose to appear by video or phone, you must be continuously connected to Zoom
21
from 8:50 a.m. until 12:00 p.m. or until your hearing is concluded (or from 1:20 p.m. until 4:30 p.m.
22
or until your hearing is concluded, if your hearing is scheduled to start at 1:30 p.m.). If you fail to
23
appear in-person, by video, or phone, the Court may proceed with the hearing in your absence. The
24
Court is not required to contact you before your hearing.
25
8. If you choose to appear by video or by phone, you must comply with the Notice and Instructions for
26
Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth below.
27

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER: CHILD CUSTODY; VISITATION; OTHER: CLARIFICATION OF
13 CUSTODY EXCHANGES AND THERAPY SCHEDULING ORDERS
14 TENTATIVE RULING
15 The parties are ordered to appear at 10am. The parties may appear in person in Department 404 or
16 remotely by Zoom video. If a party chooses to appear by video, that party must abide by the Notice
17 and Instructions for Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth above.
18
19 A. Procedural History
20 1) Petitioner Mona Meng (Mother) and Respondent Matthew Brown (Father) have one minor child
21 together, Hayden (DOB 4/13/2023, age 2). They share temporary joint legal and joint physical
22 custody of Hayden.
23 2) On 6/17/2025, the Court issued custody orders and set a review hearing for 10/9/2025. The Court
24 ordered the parties to file and serve update declarations at least 10 days before the review hearing.
25 Mother filed an update declaration; Father filed 4 declarations in the week leading up to the
26 review hearing. The Court continued the hearing to allow Mother to file a reply to Father’s
27 declarations.
28 3) At a 10/14/2025 hearing, the Court ordered that the parties shall continue to share joint legal and
29 joint physical custody. The Court ordered that Hayden’s Friday behavioral therapy shall resume
1 and that both parents shall ensure his attendance at these appointments and his speech therapy
2 appointments during their custodial times. The Court issued detailed parenting time orders
3 including weekly schedules and holiday schedules. The Court ordered Father to pay $3,000 in
4 sanctions under Family Code section 271 for filing multiple unauthorized pleadings, which
5 required Mother to incur additional attorney fees. The Court admonished Father to follow the
6 local court rules.
7 4) On 12/17/2025, Father filed a request for “clarification of custody exchanges and therapy
8 scheduling orders.” He states, among other things, that based on the Court’s statement in its
9 6/17/2025 order that its goal is to reduce conflict by “working toward all exchanges occurring at
10 preschool,” he asked Mother twice whether they could extend Hayden’s preschool enrollment to
11 4pm, but she did not respond until 12/16/2025. Father also seeks flexibility in scheduling
12 Hayden’s therapy sessions. He requests that all custody exchanges occur at Hayden’s preschool
13 when school is open; that Mother not unreasonably withhold authorization for any no-cost steps
14 necessary to allow Hayden to remain enrolled through the exchange time on exchange days; that
15 therapy sessions during a parent’s custodial time be scheduled and managed by the custodial
16 parent; and that both parties shall accept a morning therapy slot if offered.
17 5) On 1/13/2026, Father filed a supplemental declaration. On 2/5/2026, he filed a second
18 supplemental declaration.
19 6) On 2/10/2026, Mother filed objections and a motion to strike Father’s three declarations on the
20 grounds that the declarations total 84 pages in violation of local court rules. She states it is the
21 fifth time Father has violated the local rules and the third time Mother has had to object and move
22 to strike his pleadings. Mother seeks sanctions under Family Code section 271.
23 7) On 2/17/2026, Mother filed a declaration stating, among other things, that Hayden lives primarily
24 with her and that she is responsible for his daily care, school attendance, and the coordination and
25 transportation for his therapeutic services during her custodial time. She states she would like to
26 keep the current parenting time order, which began in January 2026, in place.
27 8) On 2/19/2026, Father filed a fourth declaration.
28 9) On 2/20/2026, Mother filed a responsive declaration in which she states it is not possible for
29 custody exchanges to occur at the preschool based on Hayden’s court-ordered preschool hours.
1 She notes that Father previously sought to extend Hayden’s preschool hours and that the Court
2 did not order it. In addition, Mother requests some changes to the current custody order,
3 including splitting the Thanksgiving break into half so that each party has half the week with
4 Hayden.
5 10) On 2/23/2026, Father filed a reply declaration.
6 B. Findings and Orders
7 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
8 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
9 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
10 child is the United States.
11 2) The parties are ordered to appear at 10am on 3/5/2026 in Department 404, in person or by
12 Zoom video.

22 A. Procedural History
23 1) Petitioner Emily DeLarre (Mother) and Respondent Justin Ward (Father) have one minor child
24 together, Chloe (DOB 7/15/2024, age 1).
25 2) On 12/11/2024, the Court denied Mother’s request for a Domestic Violence Restraining Order
26 and awarded the parties joint legal and joint physical custody. The Court awarded Father daytime
27 parenting time and increased his parenting time at a 2/20/2025 review hearing. On 9/9/2025, the
28 Court increased Father’s parenting time and issued other orders including a holiday schedule,
29 child support, and sanctions.
1 3) On 12/4/2025, Father filed a request for a change in parenting time, an order for daycare re-
2 enrollment, an order removing the previously court-ordered temporary dairy restriction, and
3 sanctions under Family Code section 271. He states that the parties’ current parenting time
4 schedule has created instability; he believes that fewer transitions and a predictable daily structure
5 would be in Chloe’s best interests. He states Chloe has been out of daycare for two months due to
6 Mother’s behavior, and he seeks sanctions based on what he alleges is Mother’s “ongoing pattern
7 of high-conflict behavior.”
8 4) On 12/18/2025, Mother filed an ex parte request for emergency orders relating to Chloe’s daycare
9 hours. Father filed a response. The Court ordered that on a temporary basis, until Father’s request
10 for order is heard, Chloe shall attend daycare Monday through Friday, 9am to 4pm, with each
11 party having one day during their custodial time in which they may pick up Chloe at 3pm.
12 5) On 2/19/2026, Mother filed a responsive declaration in which she asks the Court to maintain the
13 current parenting time schedule. She seeks an order for Father to follow all medical provider’s
14 recommendations for reintroduction of dairy products and to not transport Chloe on a bicycle or
15 any other mode of transportation without a helmet or other legally required safety equipment. As
16 to daycare, she asks the Court to adopt the 12/18/2025 emergency orders as permanent orders.
17 She asks the Court to adopt her proposals relating to a holiday schedule, holiday travel, and
18 Spring Break 2026 travel. She asks the Court to deny Father’s request for sanctions under Family
19 Code section 271 and to grant her request for $4,450 in sanctions against Father.
20 6) On 2/26/2026, Father filed a reply declaration and a declaration totaling 123 pages including
21 exhibits. On 3/2/2026, Mother filed objections and a motion to strike any mention of, or reference
22 to, or inclusion of Exhibits G, R, and S as inadmissible hearsay, and to strike pages 6 through 13
23 of the declaration as exceeding the 5-page limit for reply declarations.
24 B. Findings and Orders
25 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
26 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
27 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
28 child is the United States.
29
1 2) The parties are ordered to appear at 11am on 3/5/2026 in Department 404, in person or by
2 Zoom video.

19 A. Procedural History
20 1) Petitioner Arescia Yohana Meija Lopez (Mother) and Respondent Maynor Enrique Mikery
21 Castro (Father) have two minor children together, Jeremy (DOB 4/27/2019, age 6) and Valerie
22 (DOB 1/6/2023, age 3).
23 2) On 12/3/2025, Mother filed a request for sole legal custody and sole physical custody to her, with
24 no parenting time for Father. She states there is a 10-year criminal protective order against Father
25 that expires in June 2033 and that the children live with her. She states that Father is "a very
26 violent man and an alcoholic" and that the children are not safe in his care. She states that Father
27 continues to contact her from an "unknown number" despite the criminal protective order and that
28 when Mother accidentally answers the calls, he screams insults at her and does not ask about the
29 children.
1 3) Father filed a response on 12/31/2025 in which he denies that he drinks alcohol. He states he
2 completed an alcohol abuse program as well as a 52-week domestic violence program. He states
3 he is now married and has a stepchild, and he has moved on. He states he is a "completely . . . fit
4 and caring parent who [is] simply seeking to play his normal role as a father in the lives of his
5 children."
6 B. Findings and Orders
7 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
8 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
9 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
10 children is the United States.
11 2) The parties are ordered to appear at 9am on 3/5/2026 in Department 404, in person or by
12 Zoom video.

19 A. Procedural History
20 1) Petitioner Kianna Berry (Mother) and Respondent Calvin Lincoln (Father) have one minor child
21 together, Kahleah (DOB 6/1/2018, age 7).
22 2) In a 6/26/2020 juvenile court order, Mother was awarded sole legal and sole physical custody of
23 Kahleah, with parenting time for Father to be arranged by Mother and the paternal grandmother.
24 3) In a stipulation and order filed 3/11/2025, the parties agreed to share joint legal and joint physical
25 custody of Kahleah.
26 4) At a 12/29/2025 hearing on Mother's request for sole legal and sole physical custody of Kahleah,
27 Mother testified she did not understand that the stipulation and order she signed on 3/11/2025
28 meant she was giving up her custody rights. She testified that Father used the 3/11/2025
29 stipulation and order to refuse to return Kahleah to Mother's care and to unilaterally enroll her in
1 a school in Stockton, where he lives. Father, who appeared by Zoom/phone, testified that he did
2 not return Kahleah to Mother's care because he did not think Kahleah was safe with her. As the
3 Court began to issue its orders, starting with an order for Kahleah to be returned to Mother's care,
4 Father began to yell and did not stop despite multiple requests and warnings. He then
5 disconnected the call, and when the Court made a number of attempts to have him return to
6 Court, he returned for short periods of time before disconnecting the calls. The Court awarded
7 sole physical custody of Kahleah to Mother, with supervised visitation for Father through Rally
8 Family Visitation Services. The Court also ordered that Kahleah be re-enrolled in her San
9 Francisco school. The Court set a review hearing for 3/5/2026.
10 5) On 1/6/2026, Father filed a request for unsupervised visits and the request was set for hearing on
11 3/5/2026, the review hearing date. There is no proof of service indicating the 1/6/2026 request
12 was served on Mother.
13 B. Findings and Orders
14 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
15 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
16 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
17 child is the United States.
18 2) The parties are ordered to appear at 9am on 3/5/2026 in Department 404, in person or by
19 Zoom video.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER RE:(1) EDU APP AUTHORITY (LIM); (2)
13 TRANSIT/MEDICAL/DENTAL/ORTHO DECISIONS; (3) OFW COMMS; (5) TRUE-UPS & TAX
14 DOCS FOR 2024; (6) CHILD'S VOICE + MINOR'S COUNSEL
15 TENTATIVE RULING
16 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
17 Court makes the following findings and orders:
18 A. Procedural History
19 1) The parties in this matter are Petitioner Monish Bhatia (Father) and Respondent Nivita Shaw
20 (Mother). The parties married on 10/24/2011. The parties disagree regarding their date of
21 separation by one month, but agree they were married for at least 6 years and 10 months. The
22 parties have two minor children, Shailen (DOB 7/3/12, age 13) and Saveer (DOB 10/15/13, age
23 12). Both parties are self-represented.
24 2) On 6/14/2021, per the Findings and Order After Trial, Judge Chan ordered Mother to pay Father
25 effective 1/1/2021 $580 per month for guideline child support.” A two-way annual bonus report
26 is attached to the child support calculation for 2021. The following language is included in the
27 June 2021 order regarding Smith / Ostler child support: “Monish’s other taxable income from his
28 interest in his flow through entities, including any income from MNM over net zero, shall be
29 subject to a Smith/Ostler bonus support calculation effective January 1, 2021.” Additionally,
1 “effective January 1, 2021, each party’s rental income shall be allocate for support using a
2 Smith/Ostler bonus calculation on the net rental income received by both parties at the end of
3 each year.” This is the only language in the 6/14/2021 order that addresses Smith / Ostler child
4 support.
5 3) A Judgment dissolving the parties marriage was entered on 8/19/2021.
6 4) At the hearing on 2/9/2023, Judge Flores adopted his Tentative Ruling regarding various issues,
7 including child support. Included in these orders is the following: “The Court denies Petitioner’s
8 request for a modification of the 6/14/2021 child support order... Modifications of permanent
9 child support orders require the moving party to show a change in circumstance. As his change of
10 circumstances, Petitioner alleges that Respondent’s rental income has increased. Petitioner has
11 not met his burden in proving that Respondent’s rental income has increased. The evidence as
12 presented to the Court suggests that Petitioner is still losing money on her rental properties, just
13 as she was when the 6/14/2021 order was submitted. Therefore, all requests to modify the
14 6/14/2021 are denied without prejudice… Petitioner’s request for Respondent to provide
15 documentation of her 2021 rental income and final pay stub for 2021 is denied without prejudice.
16 The 6/14/2021 does not provide a procedure requiring the parties to exchange this information,
17 and therefore the Court does not appear to have the authority to order the exchange. Respondent’s
18 requests for financial information are denied for the same reason. In an effort to provide a
19 structure for the parties to avoid a similar dispute in the future, the Court orders the following: a.
20 Commencing January 1, 2023, the parties shall conduct an annual true up to calculate any support
21 arrearages that may be owed between the parties for the previous calendar year. The true up shall
22 occur by May 15th of each year. Each party shall provide to the other a copy of all tax forms
23 submitted to the government for the previous year, along with any tax returns if they are
24 available. Any support that may be owed after the true up calculation shall be paid no later than
25 June 30th of each year. The Court encourages the parties to retain a neutral 3rd party to conduct
26 the true up each year and reduce conflict between the parties. b. The parties shall conduct a true
27 up for calendar year 2021 and 2022 in 2023 according to the above schedule.”
28 5) Now on for hearing is Father’s Request for Order filed 8/26/2025, wherein Father requests that
29 the Court order Mother to “Provide 2024 returns (all schedules) + final 2024 pay stub within 10
1 days; pay past-due $8,109 (2021-2023) within 10 days; complete 2024 true-up per order; mark
2 reimbursements paid in OFW.”
6) At the prior 12/16/2025 hearing (per the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 1/5/2026), the
3
Court ordered the parties to exchange their 2024 tax returns (including all schedules) and their
4
final, end-of-year paystub for 2024 no later than 12/26/2025 and then continued the hearing to
5
3/5/2026. The Court also ordered Father to explain the bases for his requests and to state whether
6
he will agree to use a joint neutral accountant to assist the parties to true up child support for 2021
7
– 2024. The Court ordered Mother to file a Responsive Declaration and Father to file a Reply
8
Declaration.
9
7) On 2/9/2026, Father filed a Declaration. Father states that based on his calculations, Mother owes
10
him child support of $11,343 for the period 2021 – 2024. Father states that he has performed a
11
reconciliation in good faith that is fully documented and source-verified and a joint neutral
12
accountant is unnecessary and the expense would be disproportionate to the amount owed. Father
13
also states that Mother does not mark reimbursements as “sent” or “paid” in OurFamilyWizard
14
and makes payments vis USPS checks sent by mail which do not include identifying information
15
(e.g., request number, expense category, or period covered). Father asks that the Court order
16
Mother to use OurFamilyWizard Pay, or other electronic payment means, or wage assignment to
17
ensure payment documentation, accurate reconciliation, and timely payments. Father states that
18
he now pays the children’s health insurance premiums even though this is not reflected in the
19
2021 Dissomaster and Father “reserves the right to seek modification on this issue.”
20
8) On 2/20/2026, Mother filed a Responsive Declaration. Mother states that she is hesitant to take
21
Father at his word because she was not provided full tax returns for 2021, 2022, and 2023.
22
Mother states that she has fully complied with all child support and reimbursement orders and
23
will continue to comply with true up payments. Mother asks the Court to order a joint neutral
24
accountant to review all tax documentation to determine child support true up for 2021 – 2024
25
and for future years. Mother also states that she prefers to continue sending checks to Father
26
directly from her bank with a postmark on the envelope and dates on the checks. Mother also
27
states that regarding the children’s health insurance premiums, she began automatically paying
28
reimbursements for these in 2025.
29
1 9) On 2/26/2026, Father filed a Reply Declaration reiterating all of his original requests.
2 B. Findings and Order
3 1) The Court notes that a Findings and Order After Hearing was never filed to memorialize Judge
4 Flores’ 2/9/2023 order. On the Court’s own motion, the Court will forthwith file and mail to the
5 parties a Findings and Order After Hearing for the 2/9/2023 hearing date.
6 2) The Findings and Order After Trial filed 6/14/2021 (which has not been modified to date) states,
7 “effective January 1, 2021, each party’s rental income shall be allocate for support using a
8 Smith/Ostler bonus calculation on the net rental income received by both parties at the end of
9 each year.” According to Father’s 2/9/2026 declaration, both parties reported net rental income
10 losses in 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024. On this basis, the Court finds that neither party owes the
11 other Smith / Ostler child support for 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024.
12 3) The Findings and Order After Trial filed 6/14/2021 also states, “Monish’s other taxable income
13 from his interest in his flow through entities, including any income from MNM over net zero,
14 shall be subject to a Smith/Ostler bonus support calculation effective January 1, 2021.” Father
15 states that in 2021 and 2022, he did not earn positive income through MNM. In 2023, Father
16 states that he earned $4,933 in net positive income for MNM and in 2024, Father states that he
17 earned $17,200 in net positive income for MNM. According to the bonus table attached to the
18 6/14/2021 order, Father owes Mother $421 for Smith / Ostler child support for 2023 and $1,888
19 for Smith / Ostler child support for 2024. Father shall pay to Mother the total of $2,309 no later
20 than 3/15/2026.
21 4) There is no Smith / Ostler order currently in effect which requires either party to pay Smith /
22 Ostler child support on any other sources of income. Therefore, to the extent Father is requesting
23 Smith / Ostler child support for any other source of income (other than the parties’ net rental

2 1) The Court finds that Wife did not meet her burden to prove her claim that Husband owes her
3 $121,000 from the house sale proceeds. Wife provided no documentation or timeline regarding
4 the following expenses she states should have been split: homeowners insurance ($11K),
5 mortgage ($80K), and upgrades to the bathrooms and yard ($74K). Moreover, the Court finds that
